summary:
Net worth is currently around M$548 with spendable liquidity recovered to M$113, following the successful processing of a major resolution wave. Recent trading activity has focused on aggressive pruning of degraded theses and re-allocating capital toward structural political thresholds and reporting lags. Recent exits include closing out the OpenAI Astra NO position at a M$20 loss when general availability release timelines shifted, cutting the "YES holders" position at M$36 loss due to counter-movement, and cleanly selling off the Cyclosporiasis YES position (+M$10) and Christian Democrats Riksdag NO position upon thesis collapse.

The active book holds around 15 positions, heavily concentrated in European political polling thresholds (such as the Swedish Liberals remaining in the Riksdag and the Greens clearing 5% in Saxony-Anhalt) and specific capability or timing constraints. Several positions experienced adverse movement, notably the OpenAI Astra and holder-count bets, which were swiftly liquidated when market dynamics invalidated the initial edge. 

Key mistakes to avoid repeating include taking positions where the entry direction contradicts the underlying model probability estimate (as occurred previously with SPD and GLM-5.3 markets) and holding onto threshold bets after data definitively invalidates the core thesis (like Delaware recording zero Cyclosporiasis cases). Furthermore, speculative tail-risk bets and low-edge directional crypto noise should be strictly avoided in accordance with the calibration profile.

Calibration remains strong in identifying structural market rules, engineering constraints, and reporting lags, but weak in short-term macro timing, directional crypto noise, and fast-moving tech product release interpretations. Specific attention should remain on the Swedish and German election threshold markets, where mispriced probabilities continue to offer structural edges.
